statusNote: Design mapping for T00. A rule is evidence about where a call must run in Web, not proof that it works there. Each member is verified only when the task named in verifyIn ships a passing adapter for it.

classes.browser-native: Implemented in the browser with standard Web APIs or by moving existing TypeScript into a browser worker; no server round trip is needed for the call itself.
classes.server-api: Needs the authenticated server: user files/revisions, personal preferences, public settings, provider gateway, chat history, retrieval or realtime command bridge. Identity comes from the server session, never from call arguments.
classes.isolated-worker: Heavy or native processing (Rust sidecar, PDFium/pdf-lib on Node, headless Chromium export) run as an authorized job in the T08 sandbox; results return through T06 revisions or download.
classes.unsupported: User-visible desktop feature not offered in Web scope. The BrowserHost capability catalog must report it as unsupported and the call must fail closed, never pretend success.
classes.desktop-only: Electron window/shell/OS-path plumbing that the Web shell replaces structurally (routing, tabs, beforeunload, file ids instead of paths). No BrowserHost method is provided.

rules.web: Read same-origin clipboard URLs or rasterize CORS-enabled images in the browser
rules.rationale: The browser uses its own origin policy and does not send clipboard URLs to the server media gateway. The native preload leaves this override undefined.

rules.web: Local same-process inline-save byte hint; final authenticated HTTP envelope remains bounded
rules.rationale: Native preload explicitly leaves this hint undefined to preserve IPC chunking. Only the Web bridge supplies a bounded value; the hint grants no file or worker authority.

rules.web: Web shell routes, tabs and in-page menus
rules.rationale: Menu, tab, context-menu and window events originate in Electron's main process; a Web page owns its own menus and tabs.

rules.web: beforeunload guard plus in-page save/print commands
rules.rationale: Window-close and menu-driven save/print handshakes exist because the desktop main process owns the window; Web has no equivalent channel.

rules.web: File ids and uploads (T05); no host paths
rules.rationale: These take or return local filesystem paths. Web identifies documents by server file id and must not accept client paths (path traversal / authorization).

rules.web: Export jobs (T08)
rules.rationale: Desktop CLI launches a hidden editor window for export; Web runs exports as authorized jobs instead.

rules.web: Editor generation counter, beforeunload, IndexedDB draft (disabled in privacy mode, T21)
rules.rationale: Dirty state and crash-recovery drafts are local to the tab; the persisted truth is still a T06 revision.

rules.web: BrowserHost preferences + data-theme / prefers-color-scheme
rules.rationale: UI language and theme are applied in the page (tokens.css data-theme); the stored preference is read through T12 preferences.

rules.web: updatePreferences()/personal storage scoped to Principal
rules.rationale: Per-user settings and saved assets must persist across browsers and stay isolated per user.

rules.web: Principal display name from the server session
rules.rationale: Author/comment identity must come from the authenticated principal, not a client-editable local name.

rules.web: Admin global configuration only
rules.rationale: Model/search credentials are global Admin configuration; editors must not write them or log in a personal search provider account.

rules.web: getPublicSettings() without secrets; server-resolved skills
rules.rationale: Editors need the capability catalog and skills, never full AiSettings with keys.

rules.web: In-app navigation; external URLs via allowlisted window.open
rules.rationale: Desktop opens a shell settings window or the OS browser; Web navigates.

rules.web: BrowserHost ai-transport: authenticated POST + SSE, server-side cancel
rules.rationale: Provider keys and policy stay on the server; existing AgentTransport semantics are kept.

rules.web: Provider gateway with egress policy (T21)
rules.rationale: Search/media providers need server credentials; fetching arbitrary URLs from the server is an SSRF surface handled by the egress policy.

rules.web: searchAuthorizedFiles()
rules.rationale: Retrieval must be filtered by the principal's file authorization.

rules.web: Per-user chat history API
rules.rationale: project-store persists chats on local disk; Web stores them per principal.

rules.web: <input type=file> / paste -> stageUpload; read by attachment id
rules.rationale: Attachments become owner-bound uploads; reads must not take paths.

rules.web: editor-bridge over WSS with journal reconciliation
rules.rationale: External harness commands reach the live editor through the realtime gateway, not a local socket.

rules.web: None; HTTP MCP is the external integration path
rules.rationale: Zotero and the CLI talk to local processes on the user's machine; a server must not run them.

rules.web: Browser built-in spellcheck attribute only
rules.rationale: Browsers expose no programmatic dictionary API; Electron webFrame/session spellchecker has no Web equivalent.

rules.web: Browser print dialog
rules.rationale: Web pages cannot enumerate printers or driver options.

rules.web: window.print() of a print-only document/PDF iframe
rules.rationale: Printing goes through the browser dialog; CUPS/driver options are not available (see printer-enumeration).

rules.web: Export job (headless Chromium/engine in worker) -> download
rules.rationale: Desktop uses Electron printToPDF / main-process engines; Web runs the same render in a sandboxed worker for identical output.

rules.web: Browser download / in-app confirmation
rules.rationale: Native save dialogs choose host paths; browsers download.

rules.web: Blob/stream download of bytes produced in page or worker
rules.rationale: The bytes are produced by renderer/engine code; only the file sink differs. Generation location for exportHtml/exportMarkdown is verified in T07.

rules.web: <input type=file> (plus workspace picker)
rules.rationale: Choosing a local file maps to the browser file input; the bytes then flow through upload or in-page use.

rules.web: No Web equivalent; capability reports unsupported
rules.rationale: EMF clipboard formats require OS clipboard access beyond the Async Clipboard API.

rules.web: Async Clipboard API (text/plain, text/html, image/png only; user-gesture and permission gated)
rules.rationale: Degraded compared with desktop: custom Office formats are not readable/writable from a page.

rules.web: getDisplayMedia / getUserMedia with user prompt
rules.rationale: Source enumeration differs (browser picker instead of a source list), recording stays in-page.

rules.web: Apply the Web recording budget and revoke browser media object URLs
rules.rationale: The browser tracks these values locally. Desktop media arrives as data URLs and does not impose the Web upload budget.

rules.web: No Web equivalent; capability reports unsupported
rules.rationale: Installing fonts into the OS is not possible from a page.

rules.web: Licensed font assets served by the deployment
rules.rationale: Font downloads go through server egress and license review (T00 compatibility baseline).

rules.web: Bundled font assets measured in the page
rules.rationale: @genoffice/font-metrics reads font files with Node (5 of 7 source files import Node built-ins); Web must serve the same bundled fonts and prove metric parity before pagination is trusted.

rules.web: Editor route /files/:fileId -> openFile()
rules.rationale: The shell queues the document to open; Web derives it from the URL and opens it through the authorized file API.

rules.web: openFile()/commitRevision() with SaveInput, rename via file service
rules.rationale: Opening, saving and renaming are file-service operations bound to the principal; HTTP commit is the save truth.

rules.web: Authorized job; password never logged or persisted
rules.rationale: Encryption and altChunk HTML conversion run in main today (html2docx has 3 Node-importing files); compound-file itself is Node-free, so a browser port is a T07 option to evaluate.

rules.web: XLSX worker job (Rust sidecar under T08 sandbox), output via T06
rules.rationale: These are served by the native Rust XLSX sidecar; native build is blocked on the verification host (compatibility.md).

rules.web: Revision-bound workbook link metadata
rules.rationale: The gateway reads stored package relationships and cached sheet names without accessing link targets.

rules.web: Read-only data sources (T15) are the governed replacement
rules.rationale: Workbook connections and external links reach arbitrary local files/servers; enabling them server-side needs T15 egress and credential policy.

rules.web: None in first release
rules.rationale: Picking a range in another open workbook relies on shell-managed sibling tabs.

rules.web: Second window + BroadcastChannel (Presentation API where available)
rules.rationale: Presenter/audience windows are coordinated through main today; same-origin windows can coordinate directly.

rules.web: Deck session in a browser worker reusing pptx-ops; open/save through T06
rules.rationale: The deck model and journaled ops live in the Electron main process today. @genoffice/pptx-ops has no Node imports in src; @genoffice/pptx-engine has 3 Node-importing files that must be isolated before relocation.

rules.web: None; signature validity is displayed only
rules.rationale: Signing uses OS certificate stores (system-certificates.ts execs platform tools) and node-forge private keys on the client machine.

rules.web: None in first release
rules.rationale: ocr.ts bridges to the operating system OCR engine.

rules.web: PDF worker job reusing main-process code (pdf-lib + PDFium WASM on Node), output via T06
rules.rationale: Main-process PDF code uses pdf-lib, PDFium WASM, node:crypto and node:zlib. A browser port is possible later but is not assumed.
